events_in_time_windows.name: events_in_time_windows
events_in_time_windows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required output columns for the view
  e.user_pseudo_id AS pseudo_user_id,
  e.event_timestamp,
  -- engagement_time: lift specific metric literal OUT of view; here we select the common GA4 engagement metric if present in event_params.
  -- We extract parameter named "engagement_time_msec" (typical GA4 name) as raw integer milliseconds; null if absent.
  (
    SELECT
      SAFE_CAST(ep.value.int_value AS INT64)
    FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) AS ep
    WHERE ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS engagement_time
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*` AS e
WHERE
  -- Keep only events that fall within either:
  --  (1) the 7-day window ending at the target timestamp (placeholder: @target_ts_millis, lift out of view)
  --  OR
  --  (2) the 2-day window ending at the target timestamp
  --
  -- The view expects the caller to provide:
  --   @target_ts_millis INT64  -- target timestamp in milliseconds since epoch
  --   @two_day_millis INT64    -- duration of 2 days in milliseconds (e.g. 2*24*3600*1000)
  --   @seven_day_millis INT64  -- duration of 7 days in milliseconds (e.g. 7*24*3600*1000)
  --
  -- Timestamp comparison uses event_timestamp (stored in milliseconds).
  (
    e.event_timestamp BETWEEN (@target_ts_millis - @seven_day_millis) AND @target_ts_millis
    OR
    e.event_timestamp BETWEEN (@target_ts_millis - @two_day_millis) AND @target_ts_millis
  )
  -- Restrict wildcard shards by table suffix range as documented (lifted out of view):
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201101' AND '20210131'
events_in_time_windows.description: Select all event rows that fall within either the 7-day window or the 2-day window ending at the target timestamp. Keep the event timestamp, pseudo user id, and engagement time metric (raw).

visitors_who_bought_target.name: visitors_who_bought_target
visitors_who_bought_target.body_sql:
SELECT
  DISTINCT CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit,
  UNNEST(hit.product) AS prod
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  AND prod.v2ProductName = 'Youtube Men’s Vintage Henley'
  AND SAFE_CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) IS NOT NULL
visitors_who_bought_target.description: Identify distinct visitors who purchased at least one product whose name equals the target product ('Youtube Men’s Vintage Henley') within July 2017. One row per visitor who meets that condition.

sessions_2017.name: sessions_2017
sessions_2017.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", COALESCE(fullVisitorId, CAST(visitorId AS STRING))) AS STRING) AS session_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  STRUCT(
    trafficSource.source AS source,
    trafficSource.medium AS medium,
    trafficSource.campaign AS campaign,
    trafficSource.referralPath AS referralPath
  ) AS traffic_source,
  COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue, 0) / 1e6 AS transaction_revenue
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20171231'
  AND date BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20171231'
sessions_2017.description: Select session-level rows limited to calendar year 2017, preserving session date, traffic source field, and transaction revenue for each session.

visitor_first_visit_in_feb.name: visitor_first_visit_in_feb
visitor_first_visit_in_feb.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  MIN(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) AS first_visit_date_in_feb_2017
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170201' AND '20170228'
GROUP BY
  fullVisitorId
visitor_first_visit_in_feb.description: For each visitor (fullVisitorId), compute the earliest session_date in February 2017 (their first visit date in Feb). One row per visitor.

sessions_hits_products_sel.name: sessions_hits_products_sel
sessions_hits_products_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "_", CAST(visitNumber AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  date AS date,
  COALESCE(trafficSource.source, '') AS source,
  COALESCE(trafficSource.medium, '') AS source_medium,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS hit_date,
  COALESCE(prod.productSKU, '') AS product_id,
  COALESCE(prod.productRevenue, 0) AS product_revenue
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS prod
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170630'
sessions_hits_products_sel.description: Select sessions restricted to the date range (2017-01-01 through 2017-06-30) and unnest/emit hits-level product rows so each row represents a single product occurrence on a single hit within a session. Include session identifiers, date, source/source_medium, hit timestamp or hit date, productRevenue (as recorded on the hit-level product), and any fields needed for day/week/month bucketing. Treat missing productRevenue as zero where appropriate (do not aggregate yet).

sessions_filtered_by_date.name: sessions_filtered_by_date
sessions_filtered_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  date AS session_date,
  COALESCE(totals.transactions, 0) AS transactions,
  COALESCE(
    -- sum product revenue from hits.product.productRevenue where present; fall back to totals.transactionRevenue
    (SELECT SUM(IFNULL(p.productRevenue, 0)) FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h, UNNEST(h.product) AS p),
    IFNULL(totals.transactionRevenue, 0)
  ) AS productRevenue,
  COALESCE(totals.pageviews, 0) AS pageviews,
  CAST(visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
sessions_filtered_by_date.description: Select sessions that fall within the target date range (no classification yet). Keep raw session fields needed later such as session date, transactions, productRevenue, pageviews, and visitor identifier.

jan2017_session_hits_filtered.name: jan2017_session_hits_filtered
jan2017_session_hits_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session_id: use visitId to represent session_id, carry through
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "_", _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS STRING) AS session_id,
  -- visitor_id: fullVisitorId
  fullVisitorId AS visitor_id,
  -- session_date: date field from table (YYYYMMDD)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS session_date,
  -- hit_id: unique per hit: combine visitId and hitNumber and table suffix
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(h.hitNumber AS STRING), "_", _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS STRING) AS hit_id,
  -- hit_timestamp: compute seconds since epoch from visitStartTime + hit.time (both in seconds)
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime + h.time) AS hit_timestamp,
  -- page_path: page.pagePath if present, else NULL
  h.page.pagePath AS page_path,
  -- campaign: trafficSource.campaign
  trafficSource.campaign AS campaign
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` ,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h
WHERE
  -- restrict to January 2017 shards
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
  -- only visitors whose campaign contains 'Data Share' (case-sensitive per requirement; use SAFE accordingly)
  AND trafficSource.campaign LIKE '%Data Share%'
  -- keep all hits for those sessions; but ensure we output hit rows (no extra filter on page_path)
  -- however we include only hits that have a page path or any hit (we keep all to find the next hit)
  -- include only rows where hit has a page struct or other hit types: allow NULL pagePath

semantic_filters.pagepath_scope: include hits for sessions that have any hit, but page_path values are kept as-is; downstream steps will select hits where page_path starts with '/home' when determining transitions

jan2017_session_hits_filtered.description: Filter raw hit-level events to sessions in Jan 2017, only hits from visitors whose campaign name contains the substring 'Data Share', and only include hits whose page path starts with '/home' or any other page path (we keep all hits for those sessions so we can find the next hit). This is the session-level hit cohort to consider.

sessions_filtered.name: sessions_filtered
sessions_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  CAST(visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  COALESCE(totals.pageviews, 0) AS pageviews,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS(
    SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h WHERE h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
  ) OR totals.transactions IS NOT NULL AND totals.transactions > 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_transaction_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170601' AND '20170731'
  AND totals.pageviews IS NOT NULL
sessions_filtered.description: Filter sessions to the date range 2017-06-01..2017-07-31 inclusive and exclude sessions with NULL pageviews. Keep fields required to classify and attribute pageviews (session id, visitor id, session_date, pageviews, transaction indicator).

user_first_visit_events.name: user_first_visit_events
user_first_visit_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS user_id,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime) AS first_visit_datetime
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
QUALIFY
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC) = 1
user_first_visit_events.description: For each user, find their earliest visit event datetime (the first visit) and retain any device/type info from that event if needed.

visits_sel.name: visits_sel
visits_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime) AS visit_timestamp,
  date AS visit_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
visits_sel.description: Select raw visit events/records needed to determine each user's first visit date. This isolates visitor identifier and visit timestamp/date (and any fields needed for canonicalization).

inpatient_2014_rows.name: inpatient_2014_rows
inpatient_2014_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  provider_city AS city,
  total_discharges,
  average_total_payments AS total_payments
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
inpatient_2014_rows.description: Filter the CMS Medicare inpatient charges data to only rows from year 2014. Keep all columns needed for DRG definition, city, total discharges, and total payments.

drg_total_discharges.name: drg_total_discharges
drg_total_discharges.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  SUM(total_discharges) AS sum_discharges_drg
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
GROUP BY
  drg_definition
drg_total_discharges.description: Compute total discharges per DRG definition across all cities (sum of per-row discharges in 2014) to identify which DRG has the largest overall discharges.

prescriptions_2014.name: prescriptions_2014
prescriptions_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  total_claim_count AS prescription_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE("2014-01-01")) = 2014  -- year literal lifted out; ensures view conceptually for 2014
  AND nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
prescriptions_2014.description: Restrict raw prescription records to rows for the year 2014 and to rows that have a non-null US state identifier; keep medication identifier/name and the prescription quantity/count value for each record.

medication_counts_by_state.name: medication_counts_by_state
medication_counts_by_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(total_claim_count) AS INT64) AS total_prescription_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  nppes_provider_state,
  drug_name
medication_counts_by_state.description: Aggregate the 2014 prescription records to compute the total prescription count per medication within each state.

provider_cost_records_2014.name: provider_cost_records_2014
provider_cost_records_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  'inpatient' AS cost_type,
  average_medicare_payments AS avg_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  'outpatient' AS cost_type,
  average_total_payments AS avg_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
provider_cost_records_2014.description: Select all cost records for the year 2014 restricted to records that represent outpatient or inpatient average costs. Keep provider identifier, provider name, cost type (outpatient vs inpatient), and the average cost value for that record.

provider_combined_average.name: provider_combined_average
provider_combined_average.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(o.provider_id, i.provider_id) AS provider_id,
  COALESCE(o.provider_name, i.provider_name) AS provider_name,
  -- outpatient average cost comes from outpatient_charges_* average_estimated_submitted_charges
  o.outpatient_avg_cost,
  -- inpatient average cost comes from inpatient_charges_* average_medicare_payments
  i.inpatient_avg_cost,
  -- combined is sum of the two averages; lift any literal (none) out of view
  SAFE_ADD(o.outpatient_avg_cost, i.inpatient_avg_cost) AS combined_average
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      ANY_VALUE(provider_name) AS provider_name,
      AVG(average_estimated_submitted_charges) AS outpatient_avg_cost
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
    GROUP BY provider_id
  ) o
FULL JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      ANY_VALUE(provider_name) AS provider_name,
      AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS inpatient_avg_cost
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
    GROUP BY provider_id
  ) i
USING (provider_id)
provider_combined_average.description: Compute the combined average cost per provider by summing the outpatient and inpatient average cost columns; produce one row per provider with both averages and the combined_average value.

drug_claims_2014_by_record.name: drug_claims_2014_by_record
drug_claims_2014_by_record.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- drug identifier: prefer generic_name if present, else drug_name
  COALESCE(generic_name, drug_name) AS drug_id,
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  total_claim_count AS claim_count,
  total_drug_cost AS drug_cost,
  -- carry-through key to keep row-level joinable (claim_record_id = concatenation of npi + drug + row identifier)
  CONCAT(npi, '|', drug_name, '|', CAST(total_claim_count AS STRING), '|2014') AS claim_record_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
drug_claims_2014_by_record.description: Select all prescription claim records for the year 2014 with relevant fields (drug identifier, state, claim count for that record, drug cost for that record). This is a row-level cohort of claims in 2014.

ny_drug_prescriptions_2014.name: ny_drug_prescriptions_2014
ny_drug_prescriptions_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  SAFE_CAST(generic_name AS STRING) AS drug_id,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS ny_total_claims
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
GROUP BY
  drug_id
ny_drug_prescriptions_2014.description: Aggregate 2014 claim records restricted to New York State to compute total prescriptions (total claim counts) per drug in NY during 2014.

top_ny_drug_state_ranking.name: top_ny_drug_state_ranking
top_ny_drug_state_ranking.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry drug identifier and name so view is joinable; drug_name from table is treated as drug_id
  drug_name AS drug_id,
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS state_total_claims,
  SUM(total_drug_cost) AS state_total_drug_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state = 'NY' -- liftable literal: identify drug(s) with max total prescriptions in NY first
GROUP BY
  drug_name,
  nppes_provider_state
HAVING
  -- keep only the drug(s) whose NY total_claim_count equals the maximum across drugs in NY
  SUM(total_claim_count) = (
    SELECT
      MAX(drug_claims) FROM (
        SELECT
          SUM(total_claim_count) AS drug_claims
        FROM
          `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
        WHERE
          nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
        GROUP BY
          drug_name
      )
  )
top_ny_drug_state_ranking.description: Identify the single drug(s) with the maximum total prescriptions in NY (from ny_drug_prescriptions_2014), join that drug to the per-state aggregates, and produce per-state rows for that drug. (Final filtering, ordering by state_total_claims DESC and limiting to top 5 is applied at query time.)

provider_year_averages.name: provider_year_averages
provider_year_averages.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS yearly_avg_inpatient_cost,
  AVG(average_total_payments) AS yearly_avg_outpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  year
UNION ALL
SELECT
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS yearly_avg_inpatient_cost,
  NULL AS yearly_avg_outpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  year
provider_year_averages.description: For each provider and year, compute the yearly averages: average of record inpatient_cost and average of record outpatient_cost (using only that provider's records in that year).
counter_examples: For the provider whose total inpatient Medicare cost from 2011 through 2015 is the highest (computed as the sum of average_medicare_payments multiplied by total_discharges), please list that provider’s yearly average inpatient cost and yearly average outpatient cost for each calendar year in this period, where the inpatient cost is calculated as the average of (average_medicare_payments × total_discharges) and the outpatient cost is calculated as the average of (average_total_payments × outpatient_services).

participants_cohort.name: participants_cohort
participants_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT CAST(person_id AS INT64) AS person_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`
participants_cohort.description: All distinct participants in the dataset; one row per participant to define the denominator.

icd10cm_standard_concepts.name: icd10cm_standard_concepts
icd10cm_standard_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical numeric id derived from the ICD-10-CM code string (keep as string here to preserve joinability)
  cm_code AS condition_standard_concept_id,
  short_description AS condition_standard_concept_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019`
WHERE
  -- lift the target codes out as literals; this view returns only the standard concepts for these codes
  cm_code IN ('L70', 'L20', 'L40', 'L80')
icd10cm_standard_concepts.description: The set of standard ICD-10-CM concept records for the target codes (L70, L20, L40, L80). One row per standard concept; used as the seeds for descendant mapping and to carry canonical id and label.

concept_descendants.name: concept_descendants
concept_descendants.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- seed standard ICD-10-CM concept id (the "condition_standard_concept_id")
  seed.concept_id AS condition_standard_concept_id,
  -- descendant concept id reachable via descendant/child relationships (including the seed itself)
  descendant.concept_id AS descendant_concept_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS seed
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_relationship` AS rel
  ON rel.concept_id_1 = seed.concept_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS descendant
  ON descendant.concept_id = rel.concept_id_2
WHERE
  -- only consider seed concepts that are standard and from ICD-10-CM vocabulary
  seed.standard_concept = 'S'
  AND seed.vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM'
  -- relationship types that represent descendant/child links:
  -- include common descendant relationship ids; lift literals out of callers if they need different set
  AND rel.relationship_id IN ('Is a', 'Subsumes', 'Has descendant', 'Maps to')
concept_descendants.description: All descendant concepts (including the seed standard concept itself) reachable from each seed standard ICD-10-CM concept via concept_relationships that define descendant/child links. One row per (seed_standard_concept, descendant_concept) mapping to allow mapping clinical records to the seed standard concept.

participant_condition_counts.name: participant_condition_counts
participant_condition_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  ca.ancestor_concept_id AS condition_standard_concept_id,
  co.person_id AS person_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` AS ca
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` AS co
ON
  ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
GROUP BY
  ca.ancestor_concept_id,
  co.person_id
participant_condition_counts.description: For each seed standard concept and participant, indicate whether the participant has at least one record mapped to the seed or any of its descendants. One row per (condition_standard_concept_id, person_id) after de-duplication; used to count distinct participants per condition.

all_participants.name: all_participants
all_participants.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(person_id AS STRING) AS participant_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`
all_participants.description: All participants in the dataset to be considered as the denominator (one row per participant). This relation selects the canonical participant identifier for every person in scope, applying no additional demographic/time filters.

medication_records.name: medication_records
medication_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- participant identifier from drug_exposure.person_id
  CAST(de.drug_exposure_id AS STRING) AS participant_id,  -- kept as string to carry joinable id; will be remapped outside view
  de.drug_exposure_id AS medication_record_id,
  -- Map medication record to an RxCUI-like identifier: use drug_concept_id as med_rxcui
  de.drug_concept_id AS med_rxcui,
  -- related_medication_flag: TRUE if there exists a matching drug_strength record
  -- (indicates a related medication strength/ingredient record exists)
  IF(ds.drug_concept_id IS NOT NULL OR ds.ingredient_concept_id IS NOT NULL, TRUE, FALSE) AS related_medication_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_strength` ds
ON
  de.drug_concept_id = ds.drug_concept_id
medication_records.description: All medication exposure records (prescriptions, dispenses, medication orders, or mapped medication concepts) for participants. Include fields that link a medication record to a participant and to an RxCUI or related medication identifier; do not collapse multiple records yet.

participant_quinapril_usage.name: participant_quinapril_usage
participant_quinapril_usage.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.person_id AS participant_id,
  EXISTS(
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de2
    WHERE de2.person_id = de.person_id
      AND (
        -- direct quinapril RxCUI equivalence: drug_concept_id = 35208
        de2.drug_concept_id = 35208
        -- OR drug mapped via ingredient/related concept: join through drug_strength ingredient_concept_id
        OR EXISTS(
          SELECT 1
          FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_strength` ds
          WHERE ds.drug_concept_id = de2.drug_concept_id
            AND ds.ingredient_concept_id = 35208
        )
        -- OR drug is a descendant of quinapril in the concept_ancestor table
        OR EXISTS(
          SELECT 1
          FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
          WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 35208
            AND ca.descendant_concept_id = de2.drug_concept_id
        )
      )
  ) AS uses_quinapril_or_related
FROM (
  -- base set of participants who have any drug_exposure record
  SELECT DISTINCT person_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
) de
participant_quinapril_usage.description: Determine, for each participant, whether they have any medication record that is quinapril or a related medication (RxCUI = 35208 or flagged as related). One row per participant with a boolean/flag indicating 'uses_quinapril_or_related'.
